title: Police powers and individual rights
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point teaches the balance between police powers and suspects' rights, but the closest bank points each cover only one side (leg-police-powers covers powers and leg-rights-suspects covers rights), so neither teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Police powers and individual rights
card: Police have powers set by law, such as to arrest a person, to search a person or place, and to question a suspect.
Individuals have rights that limit those powers. Two are the right to silence and the right to contact a lawyer.
a suspect does not have to answer most police questions. Staying silent is not an admission of guilt.
The law tries to let police do their job while protecting people from unfair treatment. Police powers must be used within the law.
draft.remember: Police powers are balanced by rights, so the law can protect the community and the individual.

a.q: Police question Lena about a theft, and she chooses not to answer. Which right is she using?
opts: The right to a search warrant
a.why: The right to silence means a suspect does not have to answer most questions. A jury and an appeal belong to court processes, not to police questioning.
a.clue: Look at what Lena is choosing not to do.

b.q: Why does the law give suspects rights such as access to a lawyer when police hold wide powers?
opts: To balance police powers and protect individuals
To stop police from investigating crime
To decide whether the suspect is guilty
To replace the need for a court hearing
b.why: Rights act as a balance so that powers to arrest, search and question are not used unfairly. They do not stop police investigating, and guilt is decided by a court, not by rights.
b.clue: Think about fairness on both sides.

b.best: To balance police powers and protect individuals
